Photograph: Hendrik Schmidt/DPA/AP Germany Bomb disposal robot deployed after drone carrying explosives found at German airport Counter-terror team investigating after DHL plane also collided mid-air with unknown object at Leipzig airport Europe live – latest updates Deborah Cole Wed 5 Aug 2026 09.47 EDT First published on Wed 5 Aug 2026 07.37 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google German police deployed a bomb disposal robot after a drone carrying explosives was found at Leipzig airport overnight, causing alarm and the diversion of several flights. A DHL cargo plane that had been forced to abort its landing at the airport then collided with an unknown object. It later landed safely elsewhere. The counter-terrorism team at the Dresden prosecutor’s office and the Saxony state police have taken over the investigation, which security experts said could amount to a serious escalation in tensions with Russia if it is determined the Kremlin played a role. Investigators said that overnight on Wednesday “a drone carrying an unknown explosive device was spotted by an airport employee in the security area of the cargo operations zone near the south runway” of Leipzig airport, a facility classified as “critical infrastructure”. View image in fullscreen Footage by News5 from 5 August shows the nose of an Ukrainian ‘Antonov’ plane at Leipzig-Halle airport. Photograph: News5/AFP/Getty Images “A suspected second unidentified flying object collided with a cargo aircraft after it had taken off again following the previous closure of the runway. Minor damage was detected on the aircraft after it landed in Hanover.” The airport in eastern Germany serves as a hub in the transport of military goods, including by the German armed forces and Nato allies, and also serves as a base for Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines. The drone, a quadcopter with four rotors that was fitted with an explosive device, was found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane, according to media reports. Some of the Ukrainian aircraft have patriotic slogans including “Be Brave Like Kherson” and “Be Brave Like Bucha”, the site of a civilian massacre early in the full-scale Russian invasion. A Nato official said: “We are aware of the incident, which the German authorities continue to investigate.” The newspaper Die Zeit said investigators were examining several possible scenarios including an attempt by Russia to launch an attack on Ukrainian equipment in Germany . Konstantin von Notz, the opposition Green party’s spokesperson on intelligence oversight, called for an investigation to be conducted with the utmost urgency and hinted at possible Russian involvement. “Should it transpire that a state is behind this action, this would not merely constitute terrorism, but state terrorism directed against the federal republic of Germany and its citizens,” he told Der Spiegel. Several aircraft, including a passenger plane from Mallorca, were diverted due to the incident. Operations in the northern part of the airport resumed two hours later. The southern runway, where the drone was found, remained closed. Police deployed a bomb disposal robot to examine the object. View image in fullscreen German media reported that investigators were examining several possibilities, including that the incident was an attempt by Russia to attack Ukrainian equipment in Germany. Photograph: News5/AFP/Getty Images “There is no danger to the lives or safety of passengers or airport staff,” police and prosecutors said. “Passenger air traffic is unaffected.” Germany and other European countries have had a series of suspicious unauthorised drone overflights at airports, military facilities, ports and logistics companies. They have accused Russian agents of being behind some of the flights, which Moscow has denied. European security agencies have investigated incendiary devices concealed in parcels that caught fire in 2024 , raising concerns about sabotage of air cargo operators. Some of the devices were ⁠found at a DHL warehouse in Leipzig and in freight shipments in ​transit across Europe. Tobias Meyer, the chief executive of DHL, said in a quarterly results call:: “We’ve ‌got plans for cases ​like this, and ​we’ll try to make sure that the influence on our customers will be as low as possible.” Germany is the biggest single national supplier of military aid to Ukraine and has accused Russia of orchestrating a campaign of sabotage, espionage and disinformation against it, which the Kremlin has denied. Last year a Chinese national was convicted for passing on information about flight schedules and cargo movements at Leipzig-Halle airport to a man spying for Beijing. Separately, Die Zeit reported that Russian secret services were plotting an attack against Stefan Thumann, the head of German drone manufacturer Donaustahl. The report said German investigators were tipped off by a foreign intelligence service at the end of last year and arrested a Ukrainian man and a Romanian woman this spring. Thumann is said to be under police protection. In 2024, US intelligence services reportedly foiled a Russian plot to assassinate the chief executive of Germany’s leading arms manufacturer, in an apparent attempt at retaliation over the company’s role in providing a large amount of armaments for Ukraine. The plan to murder Armin Papperger, the chief executive of Rheinmetall, was reportedly one of several Russian government schemes to kill defence industry executives in several countries in Europe that have been supporting Ukraine’s war effort. The plot against Papperberger was believed to be the most advanced. Illustration: Felt report Earthquakes Magnitude 4.8 earthquake hits Victoria with tremors felt across Melbourne The epicentre was at Leongatha, 130km south-east of Melbourne, with residents reporting houses shaking just after 2am Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Martin Farrer Fri 2 Oct 2026 15.57 EDT Last modified on Fri 2 Oct 2026 16.16 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck Victoria in the early hours of Saturday morning, shaking Melbourne and waking people across the whole region. Geoscience Australia said it detected an earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 4.8 at 2.01am near Leongatha, 130km south-east of Melbourne, with the tremors felt across the city’s eastern suburbs. Geoscience Australia said it had received thousands of reports from people who said they had felt the earthquake. Posting on Facebook , Brian Morley in Narre Warren said “felt it and woke me up”, while Theresa Stevens said: “Shook our house in Garfield.” Other posts indicated the quake had been felt in Preston, Heidelberg Heights, Venus Bay and many other parts of Melbourne. The quake was estimated to have struck at about 10km below the Earth’s surface. Victoria’s State Emergency Service said the earthquake was a “timely reminder” to remember the drill to follow during an earthquake and that was drop to the ground, take cover under a sturdy piece of furniture and protect your head and neck, and hold on until the shaking stops. The Bureau of Meteorology said there was no tsunami threat from the quake. https://earthquakes.ga.gov.au/ Explore more on these topics Earthquakes news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed World Europe US news Americas Asia Australia Middle East Africa Inequality Global development

VA-95, the “Green Lizards” flying the Grumman A-6 “Intruder” aboard the USS Coral Sea. All weather meant… all weather. Intruder pilots frequently didn’t see the target, and consequently didn’t always know when they were over the target… until they started taking fire. Councilman Chris Bausch wasn’t a Naval Aviator, but as a local elected official on both the PRJUSD School Board and Paso Robles City Council, he has taken a lot of fire. Perhaps he has been over some important targets. Chris has taken fire from the local “establishment” types both while on the School Board and on City Council. For example, like most residents, he never supported the idea of paid parking in downtown Paso Robles. This caused him to be “persona non grata” with certain City employees who were in favor of the parking scheme. Similarly, he has never supported the illegal PRAGA plan to tax property owners for the water beneath their property. He always defends Proposition 13, and he supported Diablo Canyon remaining open before our Governor did the same. Notably, Chris Bausch funds his own campaign for office because he doesn’t want to feel as though he owes anyone his vote. Unfortunately, most people, once elected, become “rubber stampers,” accepting the ideas that their staff presents, without fully understanding the implications of their decisions. Fortunately, Chris Bausch is not a “rubber stamper.” He asks well-thought-out and difficult questions. His questions tend to make some staff members uncomfortable because they often expect that everything they propose will be passed easily and quickly. Mr. Bausch works for the regular folks of Paso Robles. Therefore, he frequently finds himself directly over the target, taking a lot of fire from the legacy media and left-wing keyboard warriors. Fully acknowledging that Chris Bausch is 100% human just like all of us, he deserves our respect, gratitude, and reelection to the Paso Robles City Council. Respectfully, Ron Cuff Editor’s note: Opinion pieces and letters to the editor are the personal opinions of the authors and do not necessarily reflect the views of the Paso Robles Daily News or its staff.
